parameters.pressure: 80 MPa injection pressure; 65 MPa holding pressure

other.binder: 4 wt.% PP, 85 wt.% POM, 6 wt.% PE, 1.5 wt.% PW, 3 wt.% EVA, 0.5 wt.% SA
other.mixing: 175 °C for 1 h in Z-shaped blade mixer

evidence.quote: The granular material was injected using a Battenfeld BA 250 CDC injection molding machine. The injection molding parameters were as follows: the injection pressure was 80 MPa, the holding pressure was 65 MPa, the injection speed was 50 mm/s and the injection temperature and mold temperature were 180 ◦C and 90 ◦C, respectively.
Oxalic acid was used to remove the majority of the binders for 4.5 h at 130 ◦C.
Then, drying took place in a 50 ◦C oven for 6 h.
Sintering was performed in a vacuum of 10−5 mbar at 1150 ◦C, 1200 ◦C and 1250 ◦C, respectively, with a holding time of 4 h with 5 ◦C/min heating and cooling rates.

evidence.quote: When the sintering temperature is 1250 ◦C, it leads to a significantly higher yield strength of 923.33 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 1002.24 MPa and low plastic elongation of 6.57%.

The main influence of the impurity contents is on the mechanical properties of the sintering sample. High impurity contents result in higher strength, but lead to lower plastic elongation of the titanium component
The reason is that the microstructure became coarse because of sintering at higher temperatures, which might have deteriorated the plastic elongation.

The yield and ultimate tensile strengths generally increase with an increase in relative sintered density (decreasing porosity) and with an increase in the impurity content [33]. The lower the porosity in MIM, the better the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength [34], which was the case in this work.
